idiom_name: hand-written fake class with a std::vector<Operation> journal
implementation_notes: Declare the collaborator as an abstract base class and write the recording fake as a test-only subclass: each override implements the operation over an in-memory store (std::unordered_map, std::vector) and appends a typed record - a struct or std::variant - to a std::vector member, because nothing in the standard library replaces this compound. gMock does not either: MOCK_METHOD generates mocks with expectations rather than working behaviour, although Invoke() can delegate a mocked method to the fake's real implementation and SaveArg copies arguments out for later verification (the cookbook itself notes that mixing a mock and a fake is often a design smell). Prefer the hand-written journal when the test asserts an ordered trace over a behaving collaborator, and a strict mock when the expectation is the specification.
pitfalls: A missing override turns the method into a new overload while the system under test keeps calling the base's pure virtual - the journal silently stays empty.
std::vector is not thread-safe; if the system under test calls the fake from several threads, guard the store and the journal with a mutex or document single-threaded use.
Returning a reference or span into journal_ lets later operations invalidate the test's view - return a copy or document the lifetime.
